subject: refactor(ssh_dotnet): use monotonic clock for elapsed-time (S6561)
body:
refactor(ssh_dotnet): use monotonic clock for elapsed-time (S6561)

Replace DateTime.Now-based duration measurements with a monotonic clock so
elapsed-time is immune to wall-clock jumps (NTP/DST):
 - _connectionStartTime (DateTime) -> _connectionTimer (Stopwatch); ConnectionDuration
   and session-stats duration now read Stopwatch.Elapsed.
 - error-recency "within 5s" checks now use Environment.TickCount64 (_lastErrorTicks).
   _lastErrorTime (DateTime) is retained for wall-clock display only (error dialog).
 - data-rate logging interval now uses Environment.TickCount64.

SSHDotNetDiagnostics already used Stopwatch (unchanged).

Deferred to Phase 4 (where the async pipeline rebuilds disposal/cancellation):
canonical IDisposable (S3881) and CancellationTokenSource disposal (S2930) — doing
CTS disposal before the I/O tasks complete would risk ObjectDisposedException races,
so it belongs with the bounded async task-shutdown built in Phase 4.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

triage.rationale: Target SSH_DotNet protocol does not exist in our fork; its elapsed-time refactor has no applicable code path or mapped issue.
